# Enough Path

> Free FIRE (financial independence, retire early) calculators and guides for readers in the United States. Every figure is in today's dollars and is computed by the same open formulas the calculators use. Educational information only, not financial advice. Edited by Asier Fernández.

Returns typed before inflation are converted with the exact Fisher formula (7% with 3% inflation is 3.88% real). Formulas, default assumptions and the automated tests are listed in the methodology.

## Calculators
- [FIRE calculator](https://enoughpath.com/calculators/fire-calculator/): your FIRE number and the age you reach it for lean, regular and fat FIRE with the same assumptions. Example: $40,000 a year at a 4% withdrawal rate needs $1,000,000.
- [Coast FIRE calculator](https://enoughpath.com/calculators/coast-fire-calculator/): how much you need invested today to reach your FIRE number by retirement with no more saving. Example: $231,377 at 35 grows to $1,000,000 by 65 at 5% a year after inflation.
- [How long will my money last calculator](https://enoughpath.com/calculators/how-long-will-my-money-last/): years a portfolio lasts at a fixed yearly withdrawal in today's dollars, with a test of two bad years at the start. Example: $40,000 a year from $1,000,000 at 3% real lasts 44.1 years.
- [Net worth by age calculator](https://enoughpath.com/calculators/net-worth-by-age/): your percentile among US families your age, from the Federal Reserve's 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances (median for all families: $216,100).

## Guides
- [What is FIRE? Financial independence in numbers](https://enoughpath.com/fire-basics/what-is-fire/): What financial independence means, the five versions and how much each one costs.
- [The 4% rule explained](https://enoughpath.com/fire-basics/4-percent-rule/): Where the 4% rule comes from, how long a portfolio lasts at each rate and what the rule leaves out.
- [How to calculate your FIRE number](https://enoughpath.com/fire-basics/fire-number/): The formula, three worked examples, a table by spending level and how other income lowers it.
- [Lean, regular, fat, coast and barista FIRE compared](https://enoughpath.com/fire-basics/lean-fat-coast-barista-fire/): All five types for the same household: portfolio needed, age reached and what each one asks of you.
- [Coast FIRE: how much you need by age](https://enoughpath.com/fire-by-age/coast-fire/): What coast FIRE means and the amount you need at 25, 30, 35, 40 and 45.
- [Net worth by age in 2025: what the Fed's new survey shows](https://enoughpath.com/fire-by-age/net-worth-by-age-2025/): Median and average net worth by age from the Federal Reserve's 2025 survey, and what changed since 2022.
- [How long will $1 million last in retirement?](https://enoughpath.com/withdrawal-strategies/how-long-will-1-million-last/): Years $1 million lasts by withdrawal and return, for $500,000 and $2 million too, and what two bad years at the start do.
- [How much do you need to retire at 40?](https://enoughpath.com/fire-by-age/retire-at-40/): The portfolio you need by spending level for a 50-year retirement, what it takes to save it and how to bridge to 59½.
- [Can you retire at 50 with $1, $2 or $3 million?](https://enoughpath.com/fire-by-age/retire-at-50-with-1-2-3-million/): What $1M, $2M and $3M pay each year from 50, how long each lasts at each spending level and what Social Security adds.
- [How much do I need to retire?](https://enoughpath.com/fire-basics/how-much-do-i-need-to-retire/): Spending minus other income, divided by a withdrawal rate that fits the length of your retirement, with a table by spending.
- [Average retirement savings by age in 2025](https://enoughpath.com/fire-by-age/average-retirement-savings-by-age/): Median and average 401(k) and IRA balances by age from the Fed's 2025 survey, and the share of families with any account.
- [How many millionaires are in the US?](https://enoughpath.com/fire-by-age/how-many-millionaires-in-the-us/): Families with $1 million or more in net worth, by age and above $2, $5 and $10 million, from the Fed's 2025 survey.
- [The rule of 55, explained](https://enoughpath.com/taxes-and-accounts/rule-of-55/): How the IRS exception for leaving a job at 55 works, which accounts it covers and what it does not do.
- [72(t) SEPP rules, explained](https://enoughpath.com/taxes-and-accounts/72t-sepp/): The IRS methods, the rate cap, the 5-year-or-59½ rule and what breaking the schedule costs.
- [The Roth conversion ladder, explained](https://enoughpath.com/taxes-and-accounts/roth-conversion-ladder/): Convert, wait five years, withdraw: how the ladder works under the IRS rules, with a five-year example.
- [Sequence of returns risk, explained](https://enoughpath.com/withdrawal-strategies/sequence-of-returns-risk/): Same average return, different order: why a bad start does more damage, with the numbers and ways to manage it.
- [Can I retire with $500K?](https://enoughpath.com/withdrawal-strategies/can-i-retire-with-500k/): What $500,000 pays a year, how long it lasts at each spending level and what Social Security adds.
- [Safe withdrawal rate by retirement length](https://enoughpath.com/withdrawal-strategies/safe-withdrawal-rate/): Starting withdrawal rates for 30 to 50-year retirements, what they assume and what they mean for your portfolio.
- [Fat FIRE: how much you need](https://enoughpath.com/fire-by-age/fat-fire/): The portfolio for a generous early retirement, from $100,000 to $250,000 a year, and the saving it takes.
- [Barista FIRE, explained](https://enoughpath.com/fire-by-age/barista-fire/): Part-time income plus a smaller portfolio: the formula, worked examples and how it compares with coast FIRE.
- [Lean FIRE: how much you need](https://enoughpath.com/fire-by-age/lean-fire/): The portfolio for a minimal early-retirement budget, how fast saving gets you there and what makes it fragile.
- [How much should I have saved by 30, 40, 50 and 60?](https://enoughpath.com/fire-by-age/how-much-should-i-have-saved-by-age/): Fidelity's salary multiples by age, what US families actually hold and a target from your own spending.
- [How much do I need to retire at 55?](https://enoughpath.com/fire-by-age/retire-at-55/): The portfolio for a 40-year retirement by spending level, with the rule of 55 and Social Security.
- [How much do I need to retire at 60?](https://enoughpath.com/fire-by-age/retire-at-60/): The portfolio for a 35-year retirement by spending level, with Social Security from 62 or 67.
- [Can I retire at 62?](https://enoughpath.com/fire-by-age/retire-at-62/): What claiming Social Security at 62 pays, the savings you need and the three years before Medicare.
- [How much do I need to retire at 65?](https://enoughpath.com/fire-by-age/retire-at-65/): Savings for a 30-year retirement by spending level, with Medicare and the Social Security claiming choice.
- [How much do I need to retire at 45?](https://enoughpath.com/fire-by-age/retire-at-45/): The portfolio for a 50-year retirement by spending level, the bridge to 59½ and where Social Security fits.
- [Health insurance before Medicare](https://enoughpath.com/fire-by-age/health-insurance-before-medicare/): COBRA, the Marketplace, a spouse's plan or part-time work: the options until 65 and how they fit a retirement budget.
- [How to retire early, step by step](https://enoughpath.com/fire-basics/how-to-retire-early/): Spending, your number, savings rate, the bridge to 59½ and health insurance, with the math at each step.
- [How much Social Security will I get if I make $X a year?](https://enoughpath.com/fire-basics/social-security-by-salary/): Monthly benefits at 62, 67 and 70 for salaries from $25,000 to $200,000, with the SSA's own formula.
